review: WP4 rejected-owner containment developer adversarial self-review
scope: application shutdown, crash recovery and rejected-owner eventual-exit recovery

questions.question: Can a READY- or runtime-projection-rejected backend remain physically alive after cleanup failure?
questions.answer: Yes at the operating-system level, but it is immediately marked untrusted and enters durable FATAL_OWNER_CONTAINMENT. Its FD6 custody host and API session are revoked and a persistent application fence blocks all credential and normal backend lifecycle operations.

questions.question: Can releasing the short application lease release the rejected-owner fence?
questions.answer: No. The lease and persistent application fence are separate. Cleanup failure leaves the journaled fence active across lease release and coordinator/application restart.

questions.question: Can FAILED_SAFE return to IDLE while any owner evidence remains?
questions.answer: No. Reset requires no live child or persisted PID, no DesktopHost ownership, closed FD6, empty active and pending owner sessions, no active transaction or pending operation, and an available ACTIVE credential authority.

questions.question: Can startBackend accept an already-running backend through the alreadyReady path?
questions.answer: Only after the same complete READY, owner-session, FD6, vault authority, SQLite, AppRuntime, SecurityGuard and SecureBridge validation used for a newly started owner. A rejected owner marker or application fence makes acceptance impossible.

questions.question: Can a contained rejected owner issue FD6 PREPARE or COMMIT, desktop save/delete, start, restart or hydration?
questions.answer: No. The CredentialVaultHost persistent fence rejects FD6 and desktop mutations, DesktopHost rejects start, and the coordinator rejects start, restart, reset and normal operations.

questions.question: Can containment be cleared when stop reports success but real exit or owner recovery is unproven?
questions.answer: No. stopped=true and exitConfirmed=true are insufficient unless the child is actually dead, ownership and PID are absent, FD6 is closed, owner sessions and transactions are empty, and authority is ACTIVE.

questions.question: Does eventual real child exit recover service?
questions.answer: Yes. The controlled exit path performs owner-exit recovery, verifies the owner-free ACTIVE boundary, clears the rejected-owner marker and persistent fence, enters FAILED_SAFE, and only then permits a new fully validated owner.

questions.question: Does the crash window before the full containment payload lose the rejected PID?
questions.answer: No. A persisted REJECTED_OWNER_TERMINATION_PENDING state recovers the last backend PID from state history and restores the fence even when the containment payload write was interrupted.
